reuse.why: Every link path, the new Fintegra one included, goes through one guard and the existing findOrCreateBank/syncAccount/handleSyncResponse machinery, but the take-over unlink rewrites unlinkAccount's field reset instead of reusing it (or a local-only part of it), and the Fintegra link and download are copies of the Akahu ones rather than shared code.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount copies the whole per-provider link body, downloadFintegraTransactions is a verbatim copy of downloadAkahuTransactions, and the unlink column reset duplicates unlinkAccount's update.

placement.why: Server config, provider list, sync dispatch and link handler each go where the tree keeps them; the take-over unlink side effect is hidden inside a function named assert…, an odd home for it.

scope.why: All edits serve the four steps; the two desktop-client lines are needed to satisfy the provider-keyed records.

maintainability.why: One guard owns the link rules, but it has grown into a validator that also writes (unlinks other accounts) and re-checks existence under one flag, and the provider code it guards is copied yet again.

bypasses_abstraction.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked in accounts/app.ts resets account_id/bank/balances/sync source with its own db.updateAccount instead of going through unlinkAccount's local unlink logic; downloadFintegraTransactions copies downloadAkahuTransactions instead of sharing it.

disguised_duplication.where: The copies (Fintegra link and download functions, unlink column reset) are open, near-verbatim duplicates rather than disguised ones.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked (accounts/app.ts), created in step 1, gains the replaceExistingLink parameter and branches for closed targets, a replace-only not-found check, and a replace path that unlinks the other accounts; all six link functions still call it.
